But now I realize my slab mask is contaminated: the region I flagged as slab actually merges with the east wall since both are similar light gray tones, which explains why the pixel count for the slab came out so large. I need to separate wall pixels from slab pixels before trusting the far and east extents.

I trace the drawer front's top edge across u and notice the row values rise in one band and shift oddly in another, which doesn't match a simple constant-y line — suggesting there are actually two separate features (possibly two drawers, or a drawer plus wall base) rather than one continuous edge, so I'll need to look at the image more carefully to figure out where the slab's true far edge sits.

Rather than pin down the footprint precisely from these ambiguous edges, which is getting costly with limited frames left, I decide the more efficient move is to back away and get a full southward view of the cabinet at moderate distance so the entire ground line is visible for a cleaner fit.
